principle: Historical-place evidence and cartographic georeference are distinct. Map overlay activates only from verified control points or a verified Georeference Annotation.

profiles.title: Sheet XVII. Palestine Exploration Map
profiles.publisher: Committee of the Palestine Exploration Fund

source.provider: Wikimedia Commons / National Library of Israel surrogate

survey_geometry_provenance.source: Survey of Western Palestine memoirs, vol. I
survey_geometry_provenance.method: Sheet margins laid down on Sir Henry James's projection from a central meridian and perpendicular; trigonometrical points and sheet corners fixed by coordinate distances and checked by primary-triangle side lengths.
survey_geometry_provenance.note: This is authoritative evidence that the printed sheet was constructed on a surveyed coordinate framework. It is not sufficient by itself to infer raster pixel coordinates or WGS84 control points.

coverage_evidence.source: Survey of Western Palestine memoirs, vol. III, Sheet XVII section A
coverage_evidence.description: Country round Jerusalem; includes the watershed hills, hills west of Wady Beit Hanina, the Arkub and the Shephelah.

place_evidence.note: The Commons derivative explicitly identifies Ain Shems / Tel Beit Shemesh as a detail extracted from Sheet XVII. This proves map-place occurrence, not pixel-to-geographic control coordinates.
OpenJerusalem's archival description states that Sheet XVII shows Jerusalem and its surroundings. This is coverage evidence, not a raster control point.

georeference.candidate_control_point_policy: A point may enter control_points only after both its raster pixel coordinate and geographic coordinate are independently traceable to source evidence or a reviewed georeferencing operation.
georeference.reason: The historical memoir now verifies the survey's coordinate-framework construction, and archival records verify Jerusalem coverage, but no reviewed raster pixel↔geographic point set or standards-compliant Georeference Annotation has yet been located.
